group: q|how fast does the top 1% of cyclists ride 40 km

result.why: The question asks for the 99th-percentile time for a 40 km ride (a 40 km or 25-mile time trial) among cyclists. I could not find a credible source that publishes a distribution or percentiles for that measure. Cycling Time Trials (UK) and USA Cycling put results online one event at a time, as result sheets for single fields of 15 to 150 riders. Neither publishes aggregate medians or percentiles across events. Strava and Zwift publish no 40 km time distributions. The peer-reviewed 40 km time-trial work uses small, selected samples. Hopkins et al. 2003 (Int J Sports Med, doi 10.1055/s-2003-42012) tested 43 highly trained men on a lab wind-trainer and reports a first-trial mean of about 58:43 with an SD of about 3:17. Other studies use 8 or 9 competitive cyclists. None of these samples represents cyclists in general. No large-sample percentile analysis covers the 40 km bike leg of Olympic-distance triathlon either. The large age-group datasets cover Ironman and 70.3 distances. Roadman Cycling's 2026 benchmarks page has FTP and sportive percentiles but no 40 km time-trial values. Its figures are described as indicative, and it gives no per-metric sample sizes. The one elite reference point is the 2025 UCI World Championships men's time trial, won in 49:46 over 40.6 km. That is a single race result, not a percentile. A usable estimate would require compiling raw CTT or USA Cycling result archives across many events. No published source has done this.
